top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a mature, well-understood and cleanly attributed achievement: the magic-wavelength idea is a simple, general mechanism that was identified by a small number of people and realised experimentally at the 10^-18 level, with independent reproduction. The two-name allocation and the citation scope are defensible. IceCube is a real discovery in nature, but attribution to three people out of a large collaboration is a judgement call and the sources of most of the flux remain unidentified, so I rank it second, ahead of no award.
